Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
ARCHER COMMONS STUDENT RESIDENCES
INDIVIDUAL LEASE AGREEMENT
This Individual Lease Agreement (the "Lease") is made on June 2, 2026 between Archer
Commons Owner, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Owner"), acting through its
managing agent, Blue Heron Campus Living, LLC ("Manager"), and the resident named below
("Resident"). In this Lease, "we," "us," and "our" mean Owner and Manager, and "you" and
"your" mean Resident. Please read the whole Lease, including every addendum. The addenda
listed in Section 38 are part of this Lease.
1. PARTIES
1.1. Resident. Riley M. Torres, born 2007, student identification number on file with Manager.
1.2. Owner. Archer Commons Owner, LLC, c/o Blue Heron Campus Living, LLC, 200 East
Robinson Street, Suite 1150, Orlando, Florida 32801.
1.3. Manager. Blue Heron Campus Living, LLC, which manages the Community for Owner
and is authorized to sign this Lease, receive rent, and act for Owner under this Lease.
1.4. Guarantor. Elena Torres, who signs the Guaranty in Addendum L.
2. PREMISES AND BEDROOM ASSIGNMENT
2.1. The Community. Archer Commons Student Residences is an apartment community
located at 3800 SW Archer Road, Gainesville, Alachua County, Florida 32608 (the
"Community"). The Community includes the apartment buildings, the clubhouse, the parking
garage, the surface parking lots, the pool and courtyard, the fitness center, the study lounges,
and all other common areas.
2.2. Your Bedroom and Unit. You are leasing the individual bedroom identified as Bedroom C
(the "Bedroom") in apartment Unit 3108 (the "Unit"), a four-bedroom, four-bathroom
apartment. You have the exclusive right to use the Bedroom and its attached bathroom, and the
right to use the Unit's living room, kitchen, and laundry closet in common with the other
residents of the Unit (your "Roommates"), each of whom has a separate lease with us.
2.3. Furniture. The Unit is furnished. The Bedroom includes a full-size bed frame and mattress,
a desk and desk chair, a dresser, and a nightstand. The common areas of the Unit include a sofa,
a lounge chair, a coffee table, an entertainment stand, four bar stools, a refrigerator, a range, a
microwave, a dishwasher, and a full-size washer and dryer. Furniture may not be removed from
the Unit or moved from one room to another without our written consent.
2.4. Reassignment. We may reassign you to a different bedroom or unit of similar size and
Page 1 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

price in the Community if we must do so to make repairs, to resolve a documented conflict
between Roommates, or to consolidate vacant bedrooms, after giving you at least seven (7)
days' written notice. A reassignment does not change your rent or any other term of this Lease,
and we will pay reasonable moving costs if we reassign you for our own convenience.
2.5. No Right to a Particular Roommate. Roommates are assigned by us. We do not promise
that any particular person will be your Roommate, and you are not released from this Lease
because of a change in Roommates or a vacancy in the Unit.
3. LEASE TERM
3.1. Term. The term of this Lease begins at 10:00 a.m. on August 15, 2026 (the "Move-In
Date") and ends at 12:00 noon on July 31, 2027 (the "End Date"), unless ended earlier as this
Lease provides.
3.2. Fixed Term. This Lease is for a fixed term. It does not renew automatically, and it does not
continue month to month after the End Date. If you want to live in the Community for the next
lease year, you must sign a new lease.
3.3. Delay of Occupancy. If we cannot give you possession of the Bedroom on the Move-In
Date because of construction, repairs, or a prior resident's holdover, your rent will be reduced by
one-thirtieth (1/30) of the monthly installment for each day of delay, and we will provide
temporary housing at no cost to you. If the delay lasts more than fourteen (14) days, you may
end this Lease by written notice to us before possession is offered, and we will refund all rent,
fees, and deposits you have paid.
3.4. Early Move-In. If we allow you to move in before the Move-In Date, you will pay $30.00
per day for each day of early occupancy, and all terms of this Lease will apply during that time.
4. RENT AND INSTALLMENTS
4.1. Total Rent. The total rent for the Lease term is $10,788.00 ("Total Rent"). Total Rent is a
single amount for the whole term. For your convenience, you may pay Total Rent in twelve (12)
monthly installments of $899.00 each.
4.2. Due Date. The first installment is due on or before the Move-In Date and is not prorated.
Each later installment is due on or before the first (1st) day of each month from September 2026
through July 2027. You must pay each installment on time and in full, without any deduction,
and without demand by us.
4.3. Rent Is Per Bedroom. Your rent is for your Bedroom and your share of the common areas
only. You are not responsible for the rent of any Roommate, and no Roommate is responsible
Page 2 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
for yours.
4.4. Other Charges Are Additional Rent. All charges you owe under this Lease other than
installments of Total Rent, including late charges, utility overage charges, damage charges, and
service charges, are "Additional Rent." Additional Rent is due on the first day of the month after
we bill it, unless this Lease says otherwise.
4.5. How We Apply Payments. We will apply each payment first to unpaid Additional Rent,
then to unpaid installments of Total Rent, in the order they became due, no matter what is
written on the payment.
5. LATE CHARGES AND RETURNED PAYMENTS
5.1. Late Charges. If any installment is not received in full by 11:59 p.m. on the third (3rd) day
of the month, you will owe an initial late charge of $50.00 on the fourth (4th) day of the month,
plus a daily late charge of $10.00 for each additional day the installment remains unpaid. Daily
late charges will not be charged for more than fifteen (15) days in any month. Late charges are
Additional Rent. The parties agree that late charges are a reasonable estimate of our costs from
late payment, which are hard to determine.
5.2. Returned Payments. You will pay $35.00 for each payment returned unpaid for any
reason, in addition to any late charges. After two returned payments, we may require you to pay
all future amounts by cashier's check or money order.
5.3. No Waiver. Accepting a late or partial payment does not waive our right to collect the rest,
to charge late charges, or to give you any notice Florida law allows.
6. PAYMENT METHODS
6.1. Resident Portal. You may pay rent and other charges online through the Blue Heron
resident portal or mobile app by electronic check (ACH) or by debit or credit card. Card
payments are processed by a third-party processor, which may charge you its own processing
fee.
6.2. Other Methods. You may also pay by personal check, cashier's check, or money order
delivered to the leasing office during office hours or placed in the leasing office drop box. We
do not accept cash.
6.3. When Payment Is Received. A payment made through the portal is received when the
portal confirms it. A payment left in the drop box after 5:00 p.m. is received on the next
business day.
7. SECURITY DEPOSIT
Page 3 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
7.1. Amount. You have paid us a security deposit of $450.00 (the "Deposit"). The Deposit
secures your performance of this Lease. It is not a limit on what you may owe us, and you may
not use it to pay any installment of Total Rent.
7.2. How the Deposit Is Held. We hold the Deposit in a separate non-interest-bearing account
at Ameris Bank, 3700 SW Archer Road, Gainesville, Florida 32608, for the benefit of residents.
We do not commingle the Deposit with our other funds, and we do not pay interest on it.
7.3. Return of the Deposit. After you move out, we will return the Deposit, or give you written
notice of our intent to impose a claim on it, within the time and in the manner required by
Section 83.49, Florida Statutes. You must give us your forwarding address in writing so that we
can send you notices about the Deposit.
7.4. Joint Charges. If damage to the common areas of the Unit is not caused by an identified
resident, we may divide the cost of repair equally among the residents of the Unit and charge
each resident's share against that resident's deposit.
7.5. Statutory Disclosure. The following disclosure is provided as required by Section 83.49,
Florida Statutes:
YOUR RENTAL AGREEMENT REQUIRES PAYMENT OF CERTAIN DEPOSITS. THE
LANDLORD MAY TRANSFER ADVANCE RENTS TO THE LANDLORD'S ACCOUNT
AS THEY ARE DUE AND WITHOUT NOTICE. WHEN YOU MOVE OUT, YOU MUST
GIVE THE LANDLORD YOUR NEW ADDRESS SO THAT THE LANDLORD CAN SEND
YOU NOTICES REGARDING YOUR DEPOSIT. THE LANDLORD MUST PROVIDE YOU
WRITTEN NOTICE IN PERSON, BY MAIL, OR BY E-MAIL IN ACCORDANCE WITH
SECTION 83.505, FLORIDA STATUTES, WITHIN 30 DAYS AFTER YOU MOVE OUT,
OF THE LANDLORD'S INTENT TO IMPOSE A CLAIM AGAINST THE DEPOSIT. IF
YOU DO NOT REPLY TO THE LANDLORD STATING YOUR OBJECTION TO THE
CLAIM WITHIN 15 DAYS AFTER RECEIPT OF THE LANDLORD'S WRITTEN NOTICE,
THE LANDLORD WILL COLLECT THE CLAIM AND MUST MAIL YOU THE
REMAINING DEPOSIT, IF ANY. IF THE LANDLORD FAILS TO TIMELY PROVIDE
YOU NOTICE, THE LANDLORD MUST RETURN THE DEPOSIT BUT MAY LATER
FILE A LAWSUIT AGAINST YOU FOR DAMAGES. IF YOU FAIL TO TIMELY OBJECT
TO A CLAIM, THE LANDLORD MAY COLLECT FROM THE DEPOSIT, BUT YOU MAY
LATER FILE A LAWSUIT CLAIMING A REFUND. YOU SHOULD ATTEMPT TO
INFORMALLY RESOLVE ANY DISPUTE BEFORE FILING A LAWSUIT. GENERALLY,
THE PARTY IN WHOSE FAVOR A JUDGMENT IS RENDERED WILL BE AWARDED
COSTS AND ATTORNEY FEES PAYABLE BY THE LOSING PARTY. THIS
Page 4 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
DISCLOSURE IS BASIC. PLEASE REFER TO PART II OF CHAPTER 83, FLORIDA
STATUTES, TO DETERMINE YOUR LEGAL RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS.
Resident's Initials: R.M.T.
8. FEES
8.1. Application Fee. You paid a non-refundable application fee of $50.00 when you applied.
8.2. Administrative Fee. You paid a non-refundable administrative fee of $200.00 when you
signed this Lease. It pays for processing your application, preparing your Bedroom, and setting
up your account. It is not a deposit and will not be returned.
8.3. Amenity Fee. You will pay a non-refundable amenity fee of $250.00 with your first
installment. It pays for the operation of the pool, fitness center, study lounges, and resident
events during the Lease term. The amenity fee is not reduced if any amenity is closed for
repairs, weather, or a public health order.
8.4. No Other Fees. Except for the fees in this Section, the charges in the addenda, and the
charges in the Schedule of Damage and Service Charges (Addendum N), we will not charge you
any fee for the services described in this Lease.
9. UTILITIES AND SERVICES
9.1. Included Services. Your installments include your share of water, sewer, trash collection,
high-speed internet, and basic cable television for the Unit, and your share of electricity up to
the allowance stated in the Utilities Addendum (Addendum B).
9.2. Electricity Overages. Electricity is billed to the Unit as a whole. Charges above the
allowance are divided among the residents of the Unit as the Utilities Addendum states.
9.3. Interruptions. We are not liable for any interruption of a utility or service caused by the
utility provider, by weather, or by repairs, and your rent will not be reduced because of it, unless
the interruption is caused by our negligence or Florida law provides otherwise. We will act with
reasonable diligence to restore any service within our control.
10. OCCUPANCY AND GUESTS
10.1. Who May Live in the Bedroom. Only you may live in the Bedroom. No one else may
occupy the Bedroom or the Unit as a resident unless they have signed a lease with us.
10.2. Guests. You may have guests in the Unit, subject to the rights of your Roommates and to
the Community Policies (Addendum A), which limit overnight guests. You are responsible for
the conduct of your guests anywhere in the Community, and for any damage they cause.
Page 5 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
10.3. Guest Access. Guests must be with you while in the amenity areas of the Community.
You may not give your key fob, access card, or gate code to any guest.
11. ROOMMATE MATTERS
11.1. Shared Areas. You and your Roommates share the common areas of the Unit and are
expected to keep them clean and to respect each other's privacy, property, and study time.
11.2. Roommate Conflicts. If a conflict arises with a Roommate, you should first try to resolve
it directly. If you cannot, you may ask the Community's residence life staff to arrange a
mediation meeting. We are not required to move you or a Roommate because of a disagreement,
but we may do so under Section 2.4.
11.3. Roommate Agreement. Within fourteen (14) days after the Move-In Date, the residents
of the Unit should complete the Roommate Agreement form, which covers cleaning schedules,
quiet study times, shared purchases, and use of the common areas. The Roommate Agreement is
between the Roommates only and does not change this Lease.
12. MOVE-IN AND INSPECTION
12.1. Move-In Inspection. At move-in you will receive a Move-In and Move-Out Inspection
Checklist (Addendum M). You must note any damage or defect in your Bedroom, bathroom,
and the Unit's common areas and return the signed checklist to the leasing office within
forty-eight (48) hours after you receive your keys. Any item not noted will be treated as being in
good condition at move-in.
12.2. Keys and Access Devices. At move-in you will receive one Bedroom key, one Unit key,
one mailbox key, and one access card for the building and amenity areas.
12.3. Condition. You accept the Bedroom and the Unit in their condition at move-in, subject to
the items noted on your checklist and to our duties under Section 83.51, Florida Statutes.
13. REPAIRS AND MAINTENANCE REQUESTS
13.1. How to Ask for a Repair. All requests for repairs and maintenance must be submitted
through the Blue Heron resident portal or mobile app, under "Maintenance Requests." Requests
made by phone, by text, or in person at the leasing office will be entered in the portal by our
staff, but you should check that your request appears there. A request submitted through the
portal is written notice to us of the condition described in it.
13.2. Emergencies. An emergency is a condition that threatens life, health, or property, such as
a fire, a flood or active water leak, a sewer backup, a gas odor, a power outage in the Unit, a
broken exterior door lock, or loss of air conditioning when the outside temperature is above 85
Page 6 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
degrees. For an emergency, call our 24-hour emergency maintenance line at (352) 555-0147 at
once, and then submit a portal request. In a fire or a medical emergency, call 911 first.
13.3. Response Times. We will respond to emergency requests as soon as reasonably possible,
and in any case within twenty-four (24) hours. We will respond to other requests within five (5)
business days. Response times may be longer during the move-in and move-out periods and
after a hurricane or other storm.
13.4. Our Repair Duties. We will maintain the Unit and the Community as required by Section
83.51, Florida Statutes, and will repair the heating and air-conditioning system, plumbing,
electrical system, appliances, and furniture we provide, except where the repair is needed
because of the misuse, negligence, or intentional act of you or your guests.
13.5. Your Duties. You must promptly report any water leak, mold, pest, broken smoke
detector, or other condition that needs repair. You must not make repairs yourself or hire anyone
to make repairs, except to change light bulbs and air-conditioning filters supplied by us. You
will pay the reasonable cost of any repair needed because of damage caused by you or your
guests, other than normal wear and tear, using the charges in Addendum N where a charge is
listed.
13.6. Filters and Light Bulbs. We supply replacement air-conditioning filters and light bulbs at
the leasing office at no charge. The residents of the Unit are responsible for changing the
air-conditioning filter at least once every month.
14. OUR ENTRY INTO THE UNIT
14.1. Reasons for Entry. We may enter the Unit and your Bedroom to inspect them, make
necessary or agreed repairs, perform preventive maintenance, change air filters, test smoke
detectors, treat for pests, or show the Unit to prospective residents, contractors, insurers, or
lenders.
14.2. Notice. Except in an emergency, we will give you at least twenty-four (24) hours' notice
before entering, by email to the address in your resident portal account or by a written notice left
on the Unit's front door, and we will enter only between 7:30 a.m. and 8:00 p.m.
14.3. Maintenance Requests. If you submit a maintenance request, you authorize us to enter
the Unit and your Bedroom to make the repair during the hours in Section 14.2 without further
notice.
14.4. Emergencies and Absence. We may enter at any time without notice in an emergency or
to protect or preserve the Community. We may also enter without notice if you are absent from
the Unit for one-half of a rental installment period without telling us, as Florida law permits.
Page 7 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
14.5. Inspections. We may inspect each unit once each semester, and before move-out, to check
for damage, safety hazards, and compliance with this Lease. We will leave a written notice in
the Unit after each entry stating the date, time, and reason for the entry.
15. ANIMALS
15.1. No Animals Without Approval. You may not keep any animal in the Unit, your
Bedroom, or anywhere in the Community, even temporarily, unless we have approved it in
writing under the Animal Addendum (Addendum C) or as a reasonable accommodation for a
person with a disability.
15.2. Unauthorized Animals. If we find an unauthorized animal, we may charge you $150.00
for each violation, and the cost of cleaning, deodorizing, and pest treatment, in addition to any
other remedy this Lease or Florida law allows.
15.3. Assistance Animals. Service animals and support animals are not pets. A request for a
reasonable accommodation for an assistance animal may be made at any time at the leasing
office or through the resident portal, and no pet fee or pet rent will be charged for an approved
assistance animal.
16. PARKING
16.1. Permits Required. Vehicles parked in the Community must display a valid Archer
Commons parking permit. Permits are offered for the garage and for the surface lots, on the
terms and at the prices stated in the Parking Addendum (Addendum D).
16.2. No Guarantee. A parking permit does not guarantee a particular space. Parking is at your
own risk, and we are not responsible for damage to or theft from any vehicle.
16.3. Towing. Vehicles without a valid permit, parked in a fire lane, parked in a reserved or
handicapped space without authorization, or inoperable may be towed at the vehicle owner's
expense by the towing company posted at the Community entrances.
17. RENTER'S INSURANCE
17.1. Insurance Required. You must keep renter's insurance in force throughout the Lease term
as stated in the Renter's Insurance Addendum (Addendum G).
17.2. Our Insurance. Our insurance does not cover your belongings or your liability to others.
You are responsible for any loss of or damage to your personal property, including loss caused
by fire, theft, water, wind, or storm, unless the loss is caused by our negligence.
18. SMOKING
Page 8 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
18.1. Smoke-Free Community. The Community is smoke-free. The rules on smoking and
vaping are in the Smoke-Free Addendum (Addendum J).
19. CONDUCT AND COMMUNITY POLICIES
19.1. Policies. You, your guests, and anyone else in the Community with your permission must
follow the Community Policies (Addendum A), as we may reasonably change them from time
to time after giving you thirty (30) days' written notice. A change will not increase your rent.
19.2. Conduct. You must not disturb the peace, quiet, or study of your Roommates or other
residents, must not commit or allow any illegal act in the Community, and must not threaten,
harass, or endanger any resident, guest, or employee.
19.3. Students' Code of Conduct. Conduct in the Community may also be subject to your
school's student code of conduct. We may report serious violations to the school as its policies
allow.
20. ALTERATIONS AND DECORATIONS
20.1. No Alterations Without Consent. You may not paint, wallpaper, install fixtures or
shelving, change or add locks, install a security camera or doorbell camera, or make any other
alteration to the Unit without our written consent.
20.2. Decorations. You may hang pictures and posters in your Bedroom using small nails, push
pins, or removable adhesive strips. You may not use tape on painted walls or hang anything
from the ceiling or the fire sprinkler heads. You may display one United States flag as Florida
law allows.
20.3. Restoring the Unit. At move-out you must remove your decorations and restore the walls
to their move-in condition, except for small nail and pin holes, which are normal wear and tear.
21. KEYS, ACCESS CARDS, AND LOCKOUTS
21.1. Keys. You must not copy any key or access card or give one to anyone else. You must
report a lost or stolen key or access card to the leasing office at once so that we can deactivate it.
21.2. Lockouts. If you are locked out of the Unit or your Bedroom, contact the leasing office
during office hours or the emergency maintenance line after hours. Staff will let you in after
confirming your identity. Lockout service charges, and the charges for replacing lost keys,
access cards, and locks, are listed in the Schedule of Damage and Service Charges (Addendum
N).
21.3. Rekeying. We will rekey your Bedroom door lock before you move in. We will also rekey
Page 9 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
it at no charge if you give us a copy of a police report showing that your key was stolen in a
burglary or other crime.
22. DAMAGE AND CLEANING
22.1. Damage. You must pay for any damage to your Bedroom, the Unit, or the Community
caused by you or your guests, other than normal wear and tear. Where Addendum N lists a
charge for the damage, we will use that charge; otherwise you will pay our reasonable actual
cost.
22.2. Common Area Damage. Damage to the common areas of the Unit that cannot be traced
to one resident will be divided equally among the residents of the Unit, as stated in Section 7.4.
22.3. Cleaning at Move-Out. At move-out you must leave your Bedroom and bathroom clean
and empty, and you share responsibility with your Roommates for leaving the kitchen, living
room, and laundry closet clean. Cleaning charges in Addendum N apply to any area not left
clean.
23. SUBLETTING AND LEASE TRANSFERS
23.1. No Subletting. You may not sublet your Bedroom or any part of the Unit, whether for the
summer or any other period, and you may not let anyone else live in your Bedroom in exchange
for payment. Any sublease is void and is a default under this Lease.
23.2. Lease Transfers. You may transfer this Lease to a replacement resident only as provided
in the Lease Transfer Addendum (Addendum H). A transfer that is not completed under that
addendum does not release you from this Lease.
24. ENDING THIS LEASE EARLY
24.1. Early Termination. You may end this Lease before the End Date only under the Early
Termination Addendum (Addendum K), under a completed lease transfer (Addendum H), or as
Florida law allows, including Section 83.682, Florida Statutes, for servicemembers.
24.2. No Release for School Reasons. Graduating, withdrawing from school, transferring to
another school, studying abroad, or changing your class schedule does not release you from this
Lease.
25. MOVE-OUT
25.1. Move-Out Time. You must move out and return all keys and access cards by 12:00 noon
on the End Date. Keys not returned will be charged as stated in Addendum N.
25.2. Move-Out Inspection. We will inspect your Bedroom and the Unit after you move out.
Page 10 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
You may ask to be present at the inspection by contacting the leasing office at least three (3)
days before you move out.
25.3. Forwarding Address. You must give us your forwarding address in writing on or before
the date you move out.
25.4. No Notice to Vacate Needed. Because this Lease is for a fixed term, you do not need to
give us notice that you will move out on the End Date.
26. DEFAULT BY RESIDENT
26.1. Nonpayment. If you do not pay rent when due, we may give you the written notice
provided in Section 83.56(3), Florida Statutes, requiring payment or possession of your
Bedroom.
26.2. Other Defaults. If you fail to comply with this Lease or Section 83.52, Florida Statutes, in
another way, we may give you written notice as provided in Section 83.56(2), Florida Statutes.
26.3. Our Remedies. If this Lease ends because of your default, we may recover possession of
your Bedroom only as Florida law allows, and we may recover the rent and other amounts that
Florida law allows us to recover.
27. ABANDONED PROPERTY
27.1. Notice. BY SIGNING THIS RENTAL AGREEMENT, THE TENANT AGREES THAT
UPON SURRENDER, ABANDONMENT, OR RECOVERY OF POSSESSION OF THE
DWELLING UNIT DUE TO THE DEATH OF THE LAST REMAINING TENANT, AS
PROVIDED BY CHAPTER 83, FLORIDA STATUTES, THE LANDLORD SHALL NOT BE
LIABLE OR RESPONSIBLE FOR STORAGE OR DISPOSITION OF THE TENANT'S
PERSONAL PROPERTY.
27.2. Property Left Behind. Property you leave in the Unit after you surrender or abandon it
may be removed and disposed of. Food and perishable items will be thrown away.
28. ATTORNEY'S FEES AND COSTS
28.1. Fees. In any lawsuit to enforce this Lease or Part II of Chapter 83, Florida Statutes, the
party in whose favor a judgment or decree is rendered may recover reasonable attorney's fees
and court costs from the other party, as Section 83.48, Florida Statutes, provides.
29. RESIDENT INFORMATION
29.1. Contact Information. You must keep your email address, mobile phone number, and
emergency contact current in the resident portal. We may send you routine messages, reminders,
Page 11 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
and community announcements by email, by text message, or through the portal.
29.2. Privacy. We will use your personal information only to manage your residency, collect
amounts you owe, and comply with the law. We will not sell your personal information.
30. NOTICES
30.1. Notices to Us. Any notice you give us under this Lease or under Part II of Chapter 83,
Florida Statutes, must be in writing and must be delivered by hand to the Archer Commons
leasing office, 3800 SW Archer Road, Suite 100, Gainesville, Florida 32608, during office
hours (ask the staff for a copy stamped with the date received), or sent to that address by
certified mail, return receipt requested. A maintenance request through the portal is written
notice of the condition described in it, but any other notice sent only by email, text, or the portal
is not notice under this Section.
30.2. Notices to You. We may give you notice by delivering it to you in person, by leaving it at
the Unit's front door or in your Bedroom, or by mail to the Unit. Where Florida law allows
notice by email, we may send it to the email address in your resident portal account.
30.3. Owner's Address. As required by Section 83.50, Florida Statutes, the name and address
of Owner and of the person authorized to receive notices and demands on Owner's behalf are:
Archer Commons Owner, LLC, c/o Blue Heron Campus Living, LLC, 200 East Robinson
Street, Suite 1150, Orlando, Florida 32801. Notices from residents should still be delivered to
the leasing office under Section 30.1, which is authorized to receive them for Owner.
30.4. Office Hours. The leasing office is open Monday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00
p.m., Saturday from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and Sunday from 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m., except on
holidays posted at the office.
31. HURRICANES, STORMS, AND CASUALTY
31.1. Hurricane Preparedness. When a hurricane or tropical storm watch or warning is issued
for Alachua County, you must bring in all personal property from balconies and patios, follow
instructions from Community staff and public officials, and leave the Community if an
evacuation order covers it.
31.2. Casualty. If the Unit is damaged by fire, storm, or other casualty not caused by you or
your guests so that it cannot be lived in, you may end this Lease as provided in Section 83.63,
Florida Statutes, or we may move you to another unit of similar size and price in the
Community if one is available. Rent will be reduced for any time the Unit cannot be lived in.
31.3. Your Belongings. We are not responsible for loss of or damage to your belongings caused
Page 12 of 46        Resident's Initials: ______

Archer Commons Student Residences | Individual Lease Agreement
by a storm, flood, or other casualty, which is why renter's insurance is required.
32. MOLD AND MOISTURE
32.1. Mold Addendum. Your duties to prevent mold and moisture problems, and to report

HURRICANE AND SEVERE WEATHER ADDENDUM
This addendum is part of the Individual Lease Agreement between Archer Commons Owner,
LLC and Riley M. Torres for Bedroom C, Unit 3108.
O-1. Why This Addendum Matters
Gainesville is inland, but hurricanes and tropical storms can still bring high winds, heavy rain,
flooding, falling trees, and long power outages to the Community. This addendum explains what
we will do and what you must do before, during, and after a storm.
O-2. Before a Storm
O-2.1. Announcements. When the National Weather Service issues a tropical storm or
hurricane watch for Alachua County, we will send residents an announcement by email and text
message with the Community's storm plan, the hours of the leasing office, and the emergency
maintenance number.
O-2.2. Balconies and Patios. Within twelve (12) hours after a watch is issued, you must bring
all furniture, plants, bicycles, and other items inside from your balcony. Items left outside may
be removed by our staff and stored until after the storm, and we are not responsible for loss or
damage to them.
O-2.3. Vehicles. If the Community's storm plan says so, you must move your vehicle from the
surface lots to the parking garage, or away from trees, as directed by staff.
O-2.4. Supplies. We recommend that you keep at least three days of drinking water, food that
does not need cooking, flashlights, batteries, a first aid kit, and any medicine you need. Candles
may not be used for light (Addendum A, Section A-5.1).
O-2.5. Your Plans. If you plan to leave Gainesville before a storm, tell your Roommates and
update your emergency contact in the resident portal. Turn off the breakers for the water heater
and the range before you leave, and leave the air conditioning running at 80 degrees.
O-3. Evacuation
O-3.1. Orders. If public officials order an evacuation that covers the Community, you must
leave as ordered. We may close the Community during the evacuation, and staff will not be on
site.
O-3.2. Rent During Evacuation. An evacuation order does not by itself end the Lease or
reduce your rent. If the Unit is damaged so that it cannot be lived in, Section 31.2 of the Lease

O-3.3. Students. Your school may close its campus or move classes online during a storm. A

the courtyard, or into the parking garage during high winds. Do not use elevators if the power is
flickering. Do not run a portable generator anywhere in the Community.
